title: Environmental Triggers
equation: Net Cues = Good Cues - Bad Cues
hook: Your phone on the desk is winning more arguments than your goals are.
statement: Set up your space so it cues the behavior you want.
explainer: Behavior mostly follows whatever's visible and easy in the moment. Change what's in front of you and the habit follows. Leave the old cues out and motivation loses.
sop: Walk your space and list every cue that triggers a habit you don't want.
Remove or hide the two worst ones today.
Put one Good Cue right in your sightline, like shoes by the door.
Run it for a week before adding another.
Re-check your space monthly. You stop noticing cues over time.
equation_example: 3 Good Cues in sight, 1 Bad Cue left. 3 - 1 = 2. Higher means the behavior happens with less willpower. Negative means your space still pulls you back to the old habit.
question: Write down one thing you'll move, hide, or put in plain sight today.
closing_statement: Design the room so willpower isn't required.
caption:
Principle Nº 207: Environmental Triggers
